### Recycling: Global Connections Boost the International Recycling Industry

According to the Bureau of International Recycling (BIR), the association’s World Recycling
Conventions facilitate global connections for driving forward the international recycling industry.
Of course, this also applied to the recent BIR convention in Sweden. This event in Gothenburg was
attended by 1,750 participants from 57 countries and more than 800 companies as well as 69 expert
speakers and discussion participants.

In her opening address, BIR’s President Susie Burrage OBE confirmed “strong progress” for the world
body across many of its areas of activity. In particular, she pointed to the organization’s
strengthened advocacy push at the international level, which would ensure “the voice of the
recycling industry is heard in key policy discussions”. The attendance in Basel Convention COP-17,
the UN PACE II Working Group and the ongoing negotiations towards a Global Plastics Treaty would
reflect the objective that recycling is recognized as essential to environmental protection, climate
mitigation and fair global trade, Susie Burrage was cited. Furthermore, BIR intends to strengthen
its communications outreach so that its messages can be more widely and deeply understood. “The
Environmental Benefits of Recycling study, nearing completion with KPMG, will hammer home the
message that ‘recycled materials are not an alternative – they are a necessity’,” the international
association gave account. The study would provide the recycling industry “with a robust, fact-based
foundation to demonstrate our environmental value and to counter misinformation with confidence”.
Additionally, the BIR Academy video series, which is designed to share practical knowledge, would
promote best practices and support education across the global recycling industry.

What is more, the increasing number of companies and national federations choosing to join BIR is
seen as a sign of industry unity and trust in its work. “Companies of all sizes, in very different
economic and regulatory environments, still see real value in a strong, independent international
federation,” Susie Burrage was quoted. “It is also encouraging to see the growing presence of
members from Asia and the Middle East, reflecting a broader shift: recycling is increasingly
recognized as strategic for industrial resilience and resource security.”

It is hardly surprising that recycling is gaining ground internationally: China aims at more
circular economy, as the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) outlines – inter alia – the country’s
targets regarding its green transformation, meaning circular economy and decarbonization (page 16).
And Zambia is aiming at green growth; the African country is progressing towards a circular economy
as part of its corresponding strategy (page 22). In contrast, Cyprus’s waste
ma­nagement needs support and political will is required (page 19).

Trade shows expand their global reach, too. For the 2026 edition, Ecomondo (3 to 6 November this
year) is further strengthening its international profile, intending to attract an increasing number
of buyers, delegations, and industry associations from all continents (page 14).

We hope you get a lot of new and useful information from reading this current magazine.

Yours, Brigitte Weber

### FUTURE ENERGY NOW

# WELCOME TO SEPCO INDUSTRIES

Sepco Industries Company Limited is the proprietor, sole manufacturer and distributor of the
Polypetron™ Gen. 5 Waste Plastic to Fuel Production System. It is a turnkey solution which can be
conveniently assembled onsite at any location that meets our installation requirements and complies
with local regulations.

[Contact][8]

The Founders of Sepco Industries, working as independent researchers with academic support from the
Center of Energy and Fuels from Biomass, Faculty of Science, Chulalongkorn University, have been
actively involved in research and development of pyrolysis technologies since the 1990’s starting
with tire pyrolysis before moving into plastic pyrolysis. They designed and built the Polypetron™
Gen. 1 Waste Plastic to Fuel in 2003. It still functions today.

 

The current Polypetron™ Gen. 5 model has broken new ground in design and innovation, featuring a
fully enclosed, fully continuous system with the capacity to produce 15,000 liters of crude oil
equivalent per day, per module, while disposing of 20,000 kilograms of waste plastic.


Sepco Industries Company Limited was established in September 2018, to commercialize this innovative
technology which has been in research and development for decades.

About Us

##### THE PLASTIC CRISIS

An estimated 6.3 billion tons of plastic waste had been generated as of 2015, of which only 9% was
recycled. If current plastic production and waste management trends continue, 12 billion tons of
plastic will be in landfills and the natural environment by 2050.


Global plastic production was reported to be around 299 million metric tons in 2013, increasing to
335 million metric tons in 2016.  


It has been calculated that 275 million metric tons of plastic waste was generated in 192 coastal
countries in 2010, with up to 12.7 million tons entering the ocean in a single year. Following this
trend, the total weight of plastic in the oceans will exceed the weight of fish by 2050.


The United Nations reported that the approximate environmental damage caused by plastic to marine
ecosystems comes to 13 billion US Dollars.

Planet Plastic
[Polypetron logo Final silver.png]

The Polypetron™ Gen. 5 applies pyrolysis technology for converting waste plastics into high quality
low-carbon fuel using an innovative continuous process which produces no pollution whatsoever. Our
flagship PPT20 model is able to convert 20 tons of waste plastic into 15,000 liters of pyrolysis
crude oil which is equivalent to sweet or light crude, but of superior quality due to low bitumen
content. Our crude oil equivalent product can be used to power low-speed diesel engines, or be
further refined to produce alternative diesel, gasoline and kerosene.


Viability of our business and production model has been proven with genuine use cases, both through
the sale of pyrolysis fuel oil for industrial machinery and agricultural equipment, and the diesel
produced being provided for testing to the BMTA – one of the largest bus companies in Thailand.
Independent fuel analysis testing has proven our fuel to be of superior quality. Key markets for our
fuel include the shipping industry, and oil traders and refineries due to the high alternative
diesel yield it delivers and its qualification as "advanced biofuel".


[Learn more][9]

The Polypetron

##### THE SEPCO TEAM

Sepco Industries Co., Ltd. is headed up by a veritable who's who in the Petroleum and Energy sector
of Thailand and supported by esteemed and distinguished engineers and academics of the highest
caliber along with leaders in the banking and finance sector and numerous other industries. 


The Founders of Sepco Industries Co., Ltd. have enjoyed academic support from The Center of Fuels
and Energy from Biomass, Faculty of Science, Chulalongkorn University in their pyrolysis research.
At the National Competition of New Business in 2011, our Chief Engineer received a Gold Medal from
the Ministry of Science and Technology for “Car Tires Pyrolysis”.

# reimagine-waste

# Working to create a
# world without waste

Only 9% of post-use plastic is recycled. Brightmark’s Plastics Renewal® technology turns the rest
into usable hydrocarbons—creating a new domestic resource from material that would otherwise go to
waste.

## Our solutions

Our process produces two feedstocks: PyBright pyrolysis oil and CarbonBright. These products can be
used as circular petrochemical feedstocks to create new, circular products.

[PyBright][6]
[CarbonBright][7]

## Plastics Brightmark can recycle

[HDPE Circle]

### High-density polyethylene

Opaque, strong, and durable, commonly used for milk jugs, detergent bottles, and shampoo bottles.
[LDPE Circle]

### Low-density polyethylene

Flexible and thin, used for plastic bags, dry cleaning bags, and food wraps.
[PP Circle]

### Polypropylene

Strong, heat-resistant, and rigid. Used for food containers (yogurt, margarine), medicine bottles,
and straws.
[PS Circle]

### Polystyrene

Can be rigid (disposable cutlery) or foam (styrofoam). Known for poor recyclability and low melting
points.
[Misc Circle]

### Other

Other types of plastics.

## Plastics Renewal® Technology

Brightmark’s Plastics Renewal® technology uses a patented-pyrolysis process to convert post-use
plastics into the building blocks needed to create new, circular products—including new plastics.

 

## Plastics recycling programs

Through our strategic partnerships, we’ve developed recycling programs focused on recycling
difficult-to-recycle post-use plastics used in a variety of industries.

Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs)
Medical

We’re recycling various forms of pre-patient medical plastics—including films, mixed resin pill
bottles, and more.

We work with a local school near our circularity center in Ashley, Indiana, to recycle post-use
plastics generated from everyday school activities.

[Learn More][9]

[MRF Homepage]

We’re helping MRFs expand their recovery capabilities by recycling materials from assorted hard
plastic items to flexible films.

[Learn More][10]

We have two circularity centers: A center in Ashley, Indiana, and one in development in Thomaston,
Georgia.

## A responsible end market for post-use plastics

Responsible end markets (REMs)¹ are entities that purchase and use recycled materials to create new
products and are key for responsible recycling².

**Definitions vary by state, but REMs are required to be:**
* Transparent
* Environmentally-sound
* In compliance with laws
* Achieve a minimum yield

 

¹Recycled Materials Association
²PackagingDive: Prioritizing end markets key to taming EPR tension: PPRC speakers

We teamed up with the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary to properly recycle marine
waste—diverting it from landfills and oceans. This first-of-its-kind partnership focuses on keeping
our oceans clean and paving the way for future collaborations focused on circularity.

# Powering the

## The proven recycling technology for plastics

Plastic Energy is transforming the global landscape of plastic waste. Our recycling process converts
end-of-life plastic into feedstock used to replace fossil oils in the production of new plastics,
while diverting plastic waste from landfill and incineration.

[Learn more about us][14]

## The plastic problem

1.8B

1.8 billion tonnes of GHG emissions generated by plastics lifecycle.

390M+

Every year more than 390 million tonnes of plastic are produced globally.

22M+

More than 22 million tonnes of plastic waste leak into the environment and oceans yearly.

9%

Globally, only 9% of plastic waste is recycled, 50% is landfilled, 22% is mismanaged and 19%
incinerated.

## Our technology & process

With our patented process, plastics are heated in the absence of oxygen to form hydrocarbon vapours.
These vapours are then condensed into our recycled feedstock – TACOIL™.

[Learn more about us][15]

## Closing the plastic loop

By recycling previously unrecyclable plastic waste, we are helping create a circular economy for
plastics. Closing the plastic loop would dramatically reduce environmental pollution and promote
far-reaching societal benefits.

[Sustainability][16]

## Digital services

Optimising TAC™ recycling plants through digital innovation

[Find out more][17]

## Sales

We offer complete commercial packages of our recycling technology, including end-to-end business and
operational support.

# Powering the
# circular transition

## The proven recycling technology for plastics

Plastic Energy is transforming the global landscape of plastic waste. Our recycling process converts
end-of-life plastic into feedstock used to replace fossil oils in the production of new plastics,
while diverting plastic waste from landfill and incineration.

[Learn more about us][14]

## The plastic problem

1.8B

1.8 billion tonnes of GHG emissions generated by plastics lifecycle.

390M+

Every year more than 390 million tonnes of plastic are produced globally.

22M+

More than 22 million tonnes of plastic waste leak into the environment and oceans yearly.

9%

Globally, only 9% of plastic waste is recycled, 50% is landfilled, 22% is mismanaged and 19%
incinerated.

## Our technology & process

With our patented process, plastics are heated in the absence of oxygen to form hydrocarbon vapours.
These vapours are then condensed into our recycled feedstock – TACOIL™.

[Learn more about us][15]

## Closing the plastic loop

By recycling previously unrecyclable plastic waste, we are helping create a circular economy for
plastics. Closing the plastic loop would dramatically reduce environmental pollution and promote
far-reaching societal benefits.

[Sustainability][16]

## Digital services

Optimising TAC™ recycling plants through digital innovation

[Find out more][17]

## Sales

We offer complete commercial packages of our recycling technology, including end-to-end business and
operational support.

# Fuels & Lubricants Supplier Since 1947

As a UK leading fuels and lubricants supplier, we believe excellent service before and after your
oil delivery is the key to our success. This, combined with our expert, local knowledge, competitive
fuel prices and reliable deliveries, ensures we’ve remained at the forefront of the oil industry for
over 75 years.

## Fuelling your success since 1947

Our large customer base includes every industry from industrial and data centres to farms, marine,
construction and much more. Our vast, diverse fleet of [HVO-fuelled vehicles][82] and national depot
network enables us to provide 24-48 hour deliveries as standard, plus an urgent emergency delivery
service for time-sensitive scenarios. You can count on us when you need us most.

Whether you’re looking for diesel or heating oils, renewable fuels, lubricants, storage tanks, or
any of our other products and fuel-related services – you can rest easy, safe in the knowledge of
our team and in-house experts.

## Our environmental commitment

Crown Oil was the first UK fuel supplier to switch our entire delivery fleet to HVO fuel, and we are
the first to be [certified carbon neutral by BSI to ISO 14068-1][83] and certified to be net zero by

with our range of sustainable solutions on hand.

With over 75 years’ experience in the industry, we are committed to providing the best solution to
support your business. That’s why we’ve extended our product portfolio to include a range of
cleaner-burning products to support you in reaching your sustainability goals.

# Our Story

Eco Fuel Technology, Inc. was founded in 2012 by Swaminathan Ramesh and Himat Taank. The founders
formed the company to focus on manufacturing portable machines that convert waste plastics,
specifically non-reusable, “end-of-life” plastics into reusable diesel fuel.

 

Shortly after formation, Eco Fuel Technology, Inc. worked with James Holm to pilot a portable
machine for installation on a boat. The objective of the pilot project is to install a machine on a
boat that will pick up plastics in the ocean and convert the plastics to diesel fuel while at sea. 

 

Eco Fuel Technology is also partnering with Ocean Guardian (https://www.oceanguardian-og.org/) and
with [Ocean Recovery Systems][16] to recover plastics from the mid depths of the ocean and convert
them to fuel

 

In addition to the pilot project, Eco fuel Technology has launched several collaborative research
studies with universities based in California, Illinois and North Carolina. 

 

Eco Fuel Technology is now working on a number of projects (starting in second and third quarter of
2020):
* a 20 to 60 TPD operation in Memphis, TN
* 60 TPD operation in Alabama
* 60 TPD plant for BC, Canada
* a hugely potential collaboration in Philippines
* set up a manufacturing facility in Thailand to supply the Southeast Asia and Australia
* collaboration with Sunyani Energy, Inc and USABionergy, Inc.
* [Founders][17]
* [Advisors][18]

# Turning plastic
# waste into opportunity.

Exacta Energy USA delivers full-service plastic-to-fuel solutions that power the future of energy.

[ Explore Solutions ][24]

### Built on Innovation, Driven by Purpose

## WHAT WE DO

Solving the problem
of plastic waste

Production of high performance gasoline and diesel

Restoring ecological balance worldwide

## We license our technology so you can build and own your own PlastikGas® Processing Plant

#### PlastikGas®, LLC. will build you a PlastikGas® Processing Plant and license you our proprietary
#### plastic to fuel conversion technology. We design and build your plastic waste conversion plant
#### on your land, anywhere around the world.

[ LEARN MORE ][25]

## Our Services

• Turnkey Installation
• Commissioning
• Maintenance & Training

• Work with MRFs
• Work with Municipalities
• Buy/Sell Logistics

### Recyclables Trading

• Paper, Cardboard, Aluminum
• Global Sourcing Partners

### Fuel Off-Take

• Diesel, PG1, PG2 Delivery
• Storage & Compliance

## OUR PROCESS

## Simple processes that are easy to execute

## The Process starts with shredding the plastic waste into flakes or chips

Initial one-to-one consultation, Health & Fitness Assessments Bespoke training program planning,
Custom Nutrition plan & recipes. Weekly Progress Reviews
* No catalyst is required.
* Small amount of LPG obtained provides fuel initiate the next process, thus becoming
  self-sustaining.
* The reactor is filled with raw material and the hydrocarbons will be obtained by controlling the
  pressure and distillation temperatures.
* Closed loop system.
* You can process different types of plastics at the same time.

## How It Works

[ LEARN MORE ][26]

### PlastikGas® Technology

Plastic waste is converted into fuel using Proprietary PlastikGas® Technology

### Process Area

Transformation > Condensation > Vapor & Fuel Burner > Storage

### Six fuels are produced:

Gasoline, Diesel, Kerosene, Paraffin, Petroleum Liquid Gas and Coke (coque)

## Obtaining gasoline and diesel with waste plastics

PlastikGas® Technology was designed to use waste plastic as raw material and simultaneously produce
six usable fuels.

Gasoline
48%
Diesel
24%
Paraffin
5%
Kerosene
14%
PLG
3%
Coke (coque)
2%

## Our Mission

Exacta Energy USA is redefining how we see waste. By building on PlastikGas’s proven technology, we
offer scalable plastic-to-fuel solutions and a robust platform for sourcing, deployment, and
delivery.

[ More About Us ][27]

## About us

## Solving the problem of plastic waste

## Mission Statement

To solve the global problem of plastic waste which will reduce the environmental impact of plastic
waste and restore ecological balance worldwide.

## Vision Statement

To provide a solution to the global problem of plastic waste by building plastic to fuel conversion
plants worldwide. Establish PlastikGas® USA, PlastikGas® of Latin America and PlastikGas® Europe and
to have 100 or more plants built worldwide by 2030.

# About K-Jet Specialists

[K-Jet Specialists][32] About K-Jet Specialists

**Please email me about anything you need or want to know.** I have lots of parts including exchange
reconditioned Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators available, Auxiliary Air Slides, Auxiliary
Air Valves, D-Jet Manifold Pressure Sensors, Mechanical fuel injection pumps and much more for your
classic European car.

#### Reconditioning Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators since 1993
#### All Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators are sold on an exchange basis. We need your old
#### one back to continue our business and to supply to the next person who needs one**.**

**12 Month Guarantee on parts and workmanship (unless damaged by dirt and/or water in the fuel). We
rebuild our Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators with many parts, custom made for us, so that
our remanufactured parts meet the highest standards.
**
**We can recondition your own part if you want this to be done.**
**Fuel Distributors can be up-rated for extra power and performance on request.**

**We want your old Fuel Distributors and Warm-up Regulators. Contact us to tell us what you have.**

All Fuel Distributors tested on our Bosch KDJE-P 200 flow benches, our Warm-Up Regulators are set to
Bosch original Specifications on our bespoke test bench.

All our parts are sold on an exchange basis, unless we are reconditioning your own part. We need
your old part back so that we can recondition it for the next person in your situation, needing a
reconditioned part. So please don’t delay in returning your old part.

**All prices are in Australian dollars**

We use the best quality seals which are compatible with all fuels, although we do recommend avoiding
ethanol based fuels where possible. But we also build fuel distributors for racing cars that run e85
and our seals are totally fine with that fuel.

Many of our seals are not ‘off the shelf’ but are made for us to our specification. Our diaphragm
material is also made for us and we have diaphragms for our KE fuel distributors and KE Fuel
distributor kits are pre-shaped for better immediate function.

Colin has been a mechanic since 1973 and has specialised in European cars since 1979 when he moved
to London, England.

In 1990 Colin moved back to Australia and continued servicing European Cars.

In answering the demand for someone with a solid knowledge of the K-Jetronic fuel injection system,
Colin began reconditioning Fuel distributors and Warm-up regulators for other mechanics and offering
them technical help in diagnosing fuel injection problems.

Initially trading under the name ‘Agape Autos’, K-Jet Specialists has been reconditioning K-Jetronic
Fuel Distributors and Warm-up Regulators, and KE-Jetronic Fuel Distributors since 1993.

We also recondition D-Jet MPS, Auxiliary air slides, auxiliary air valves and mechanical petrol
injection systems. We have the experience and ability to recondition almost any part, so if you are
restoring a classic European car and can’t find a part, we may be able to recondition it for you.
Let us know what you need and we will try to help you.

Each part receives a serial number so that we can trace it’s history, when it was reconditioned,
when it was sold and where it went.

Over the years we have sold reconditioned parts to many countries including Australia, Austria,
Bahrain, Belgium, Bolivia, Bratislava, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, China, Columbia, Cyprus, Czech
Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, Egypt, England, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Guatamala,
Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Kazakhstan, Korea, Kuwait,
Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Peru, Philippines,
Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Romania, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Slovakia, , Slovenia, South
Africa, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, UAE, Ukraine, USA. So we are happy to send to you,
wherever you are.

##  chemical recycling

a clean, circular alternative

Misson

Neowaste   converts hard-to-recycle plastic waste (i.e., mixed, contaminated, dirty, co-molded, etc)
and other contaminated waste streams into low sulfur fuel products using a proprietary molecular
reformation process called Polycrack Technology. 

 

We were established to help companies and municipalities meet their sustainability goals when it
became clear that traditional mechanical recycling markets were collapsing and millions of tons of
recyclable materials were being sent to landfills--all as a result of contamination.


Contamination isn't a problem for Neowaste.  We don't recycle mechanically.  We recycle molecularly.
 And while the process description can get a bit technical, the science behind what we do is really
straightforward:


#### Plastic is made from oil. We're simply reversing the process and extracting the oil out of the
#### plastic.

Powered by

[Polycrack Logo.png]
[Learn more ][7]

## Services

[Core Competencies.png]

## The Mission

###### To make recycling more accessible and more sustainable. 

###### Reduce waste disposal costs

Waste disposal costs are on the rise, reaching up to $300 per ton in certain parts of the US. 

 

Neowaste's chemical recycling solution enables us to provide a more sustainable waste management
solution at a significantly lower cost than traditional methods of landfilling, incineration and
mechanical recycling.

 

Environmentally and economically sustainable.

[teal reduce waste costs.png]

###### Divert waste from landfills

Communities and businesses send thousands of tons of recyclable materials to landfills and
incineration facilities each day because of contamination.

 

But contamination is not an issue for Neowaste.  In fact, the technology we use was designed to
manage waste just as it comes--mixed, dirty and full of moisture. 

 

No sorting, cleaning or drying required. 

[teal zero landfill.png]

###### Generate fuel from alternative sources

Most people in the industry like to think of us as a mini-refinery.  Instead of using crude oil as a
feedstock, we use waste.  

 

Neowaste is not only committed to supplying a low sulfur fuel product that exceeds most fuel
acceptance standards, but we are also committed to supplying it at a cost that's competitive with
Platts benchmark pricing.


Fuel specs available upon request.

[teal waste to fuel.png]

## Benefits

[Icon image.png]

## ABOUT

Neowaste is decentralizing waste management through chemical recycling.  

 

By establishing a distributed network of small, modular units, we can manage waste at or near the
source of generation, ultimately reducing the cost of transporting and managing that waste.  


Although we can extract the most fuel from plastic waste, our process is robust enough to process
any material with hydrogen and carbon.  This means we can process almost any type of waste on the
planet and keep those valuable resources out of our oceans and landfills--all while creating
a renewable, low-sulfur fuel product. 

ABOUT

## Our Story

From humble beginnings to a global sports nutrition leader.

Founded in 1986, Optimum Nutrition was created with one mission: to deliver consistent, trusted, and
effective nutrition that helps people of all fitness levels reach their goals with confidence.

From our world-renowned Gold Standard 100% Whey to our cutting-edge pre-workouts and supplements, we
continue to lead the way in quality, innovation, and performance worldwide.

## Our Core Values

Driven by science. Trusted by athletes. Built for performance.

### Proven Quality

Every ON product is tested for purity, potency, and consistency to meet the highest global standards
in sports nutrition.

### Science-Based Innovation

We combine leading nutritional science with advanced manufacturing techniques to deliver products
powered by results.

### Commitment to Excellence

From the ingredients we source to the athletes who trust us, excellence defines every stage of our
journey.

## Our Journey

Decades of dedication and performance.

1986

#### Brand Foundation

Optimum Nutrition was founded with the goal of giving athletes access to the highest-quality protein
and sports nutrition available anywhere.

2004

#### The Gold Standard Era

Launch of Gold Standard 100% Whey Protein, which quickly became the most recognized and trusted
protein powder in the world.

2025

#### A Future of Sustainable Performance

ON introduces eco-conscious packaging and continues advancing nutrition through clean, effective
formulas that respect both health and the planet.

## Classic Products

### Gold Standard 100% Whey

The world’s best-selling whey protein powder, offering 24g of premium protein per serving to support
muscle recovery and growth. Trusted by athletes around the world for its taste, quality, and proven
results.

### Serious Mass

A powerhouse gainer formula designed to help you build strength and mass the right way. Packed with
calories, protein, and essential nutrients, Serious Mass supports intense training and performance
goals.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Get answers about product use, safety, and nutrition tips.

01

### Are Optimum Nutrition products tested for quality?

Yes. All ON products are produced in GMP-certified facilities and undergo rigorous testing for
safety, purity, and potency.

02

### When should I take whey protein?

Whey protein can be taken post-workout for muscle recovery or anytime during the day to help meet
your daily protein needs.

03

### Is Serious Mass suitable for beginners?

Yes. Serious Mass is perfect for those aiming to gain healthy weight or increase calorie intake
alongside strength training.

04

### Where can I buy genuine ON products?

Visit the official website or authorized online and retail partners to ensure authenticity and
product quality.

  Today
  
  ### Three-quarters of eggs produced in the United Kingdom are free-range
  
  Hannah Ritchie and Pablo Rosado
  
  Growing up in the United Kingdom in the 1990s and early 2000s, almost all the eggs in our
  supermarket came from battery hens, those raised in small wire enclosures.
  
  The living conditions in these cages are terrible. Birds get the space equivalent of an A4 sheet
  of paper. They don’t have the room to carry out their natural behaviors, such as nesting,
  perching, or dust bathing.
  
  That has changed in recent decades. You can see this in the chart, which shows the conditions
  under which eggs are produced in the UK. Free-range eggs have increased from just 10% to 75%.
  
  The use of caged hens has fallen, and the types of caged enclosures have also changed. Battery
  cages were banned in 2012, so legally, all cages since then have been “enriched” ones, which
  provide slightly more space. Still, these do not give hens the freedom and room they’d have in
  barns or free-range farms. Studies suggest that moving hens from enriched cages to cage-free
  systems reduces the time they spend in pain by more than half.
  
  And given that most eggs in the UK are now free-range, it’s possible to reduce this pain even
  further.

# Plastics Industry

## A Look at Plastics

The term “plastic” encompasses a broad range of materials. In addition, each has its own special
properties and variations when it comes to properties such as hardness, heat tolerance, and
resiliency. Nonetheless, each of them is made of organic condensation or addition polymers and can
be made into fibers, films, or objects.

There are [7 main types of plastics][5], anything from PET, used in food containers, to PVC, used in
pipes and flooring. Basically, plastics are everywhere in our modern world.

The plastics industry is a [very large industry][6] when many facets and worldwide reach. What is
expected from the plastics industry in [2023 and 2024][7].

* [Plastic Processing Methods][8]
* [Plastics and the Environment][9]
* [The Benefits of Plastic][10]
* [Types of Plastics:][11]
  * [Starting with the letter A][12]
  * [Starting with the letters C, D and E][13]
  * [Starting with the letters F, M and N][14]
  * [Starting with the letter P][15]
  * [Starting with the letters S, T and U][16]
  
   
* [How is Plastic Recycled?][17]
* [Injection Molding][18]
* [Employment and Jobs in the Plastics Industry][19]
* [Plastics and Nanotechnology][20]
* [Synthetic Rubber][21]
* [Recycling Plastics][22]
* [Plastic-eating Bacteria][23]

 


**Classifying Plastics**

There are many methods used to classify plastics. The most common method is to classify them
according to their polymer backbone. Plastics can, however, also be classified according to the
glass transition temperature or thermoplastic versus thermoset.

No matter the classification, [all plastics][24] are polymers, which is a long chain of atoms that
are bonded to one another. These chains are comprised of monomers, which are repeating molecular
units. Most plastics are made of carbon polymers or carbon polymers combined with nitrogen, oxygen,
sulfur, or chlorine in the backbone, which is the main path linking the units together. Plastic is
then customized by “hanging” different molecular groups to the backbone.


**History of Plastic**

Experiments with plastic have been performed for centuries. In fact, even the Old Testament makes
reference to natural materials that were used in the same way as plastic is used today. The exact
year when plastic was first created or discovered, however, is a matter of dispute because the term
“plastic” is so loosely defined.

The discovery of ebonite, or hard [rubber][25], in 1851, however, had a major impact on the plastics
industry. Ebonite was the first thermosetting material to be prepared that also involved its own
unique chemical modification of naturally occurring material. Yet, it took several years for ebonite
to be used to its potential.

As rubber technology was further being developed, collodion was also being manufactured. Collodion
is a cellulose solution that is part of an alcohol-ether mixture. Alexander Parkes, an English
inventor, noticed that a solid residue was left after solvent in the collodion evaporated. In his
word, this residue was a “hard, horny elastic and waterproof substance.” He later patented the
process in 1856 in order to waterproof woven fabrics.

In 1862, a new formulation was unveiled at the Great Exhibition in London. This early plastic was
created by dissolving cellulose nitrate in a solvent. After being placed on a heated rolling
machine, the mixture could be shaped. The first company to dedicated to manufacturing products from
the material, the Parkesine Company, was established in 1866. The company failed, however, in 1868.
A year later, the Xylonite Company was opened by Daniel Spill, who was an associate of Parkes. This
company also went bankrupt in 1874.

In the United States, [plastic compounds][26] were also on the rise. John Wesley Hyatt experimented
with cellulose nitrate in the 1860s. In 1865, he became involved in developing a method for creating
billiard balls with alternative materials. He developed balls made of ivory dust, cloth, and
shellac, which was covered with a collodion coating.

Wyatt and his brother, Isaiah, went on to create a process for producing a material made of camphor
and cellulose nitrate in 1870. By 1872, the term “celluloid” had been coined for the product. The
brothers went on to establish the Celluloid Manufacturing Company, which was later renamed the
American Cellulose Chemical Corporation and was ultimately absorbed by the Celanese Corporation.

By the 1900s, the use of [plastic][27] and all of its variations took off. Today, it is the most
used material in the United States industry, with nearly every product containing plastic in one way
or another.

resiliency. Nonetheless, each of them is made of organic condensation or addition polymers and can
be made into fibers, films, or objects.

There are [7 main types of plastics][5], anything from PET, used in food containers, to PVC, used in
pipes and flooring. Basically, plastics are everywhere in our modern world.

### Recycling: Global Connections Boost the International Recycling Industry

According to the Bureau of International Recycling (BIR), the association’s World Recycling
Conventions facilitate global connections for driving forward the international recycling industry.
Of course, this also applied to the recent BIR convention in Sweden. This event in Gothenburg was
attended by 1,750 participants from 57 countries and more than 800 companies as well as 69 expert
speakers and discussion participants.

In her opening address, BIR’s President Susie Burrage OBE confirmed “strong progress” for the world
body across many of its areas of activity. In particular, she pointed to the organization’s
strengthened advocacy push at the international level, which would ensure “the voice of the
recycling industry is heard in key policy discussions”. The attendance in Basel Convention COP-17,
the UN PACE II Working Group and the ongoing negotiations towards a Global Plastics Treaty would
reflect the objective that recycling is recognized as essential to environmental protection, climate
mitigation and fair global trade, Susie Burrage was cited. Furthermore, BIR intends to strengthen
its communications outreach so that its messages can be more widely and deeply understood. “The
Environmental Benefits of Recycling study, nearing completion with KPMG, will hammer home the
message that ‘recycled materials are not an alternative – they are a necessity’,” the international
association gave account. The study would provide the recycling industry “with a robust, fact-based
foundation to demonstrate our environmental value and to counter misinformation with confidence”.
Additionally, the BIR Academy video series, which is designed to share practical knowledge, would
promote best practices and support education across the global recycling industry.

What is more, the increasing number of companies and national federations choosing to join BIR is
seen as a sign of industry unity and trust in its work. “Companies of all sizes, in very different
economic and regulatory environments, still see real value in a strong, independent international
federation,” Susie Burrage was quoted. “It is also encouraging to see the growing presence of
members from Asia and the Middle East, reflecting a broader shift: recycling is increasingly
recognized as strategic for industrial resilience and resource security.”

It is hardly surprising that recycling is gaining ground internationally: China aims at more
circular economy, as the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) outlines – inter alia – the country’s
targets regarding its green transformation, meaning circular economy and decarbonization (page 16).
And Zambia is aiming at green growth; the African country is progressing towards a circular economy
as part of its corresponding strategy (page 22). In contrast, Cyprus’s waste
ma­nagement needs support and political will is required (page 19).

Trade shows expand their global reach, too. For the 2026 edition, Ecomondo (3 to 6 November this
year) is further strengthening its international profile, intending to attract an increasing number
of buyers, delegations, and industry associations from all continents (page 14).

We hope you get a lot of new and useful information from reading this current magazine.

Yours, Brigitte Weber

# We recycle
# "unrecyclable"
# plastic

Resynergi converts waste plastic that has traditionally been landfilled or incinerated into valuable
PyOil, a feedstock for new, high quality plastic products.

## Plastic waste Resynergi will take:

[HDPE plastic products] [HDPE recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #2

High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE)

Common Products

Milk jugs, shampoo bottles, patio chairs

[LDPE plastic products] [LDPE recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #4

Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE)

Common Products

Grocery bags, shrink film, flexible packaging

[PP plastic products] [PP recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #5

Polypropylene (PP)

Common Products

Yogurt cups, bottle caps, straws, medicine bottles

[PS plastic products] [PS recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #6

Polystyrene (PS)

Common Products

Styrofoam cups, egg cartons, disposable cutlery

The Problem

The above categories represent the **majority** of post-consumer plastic waste.

## Only 9% of plastic waste gets recycled today.

We're here to change that.

0%

Predicted increase
in global plastic waste by 2060

OECD, 2022 Report

The Solution

What is PyOil?

PyOil is a liquid hydrocarbon that can be used as a drop-in replacement for crude oil, to make new
plastic. The name comes from the word "pyrolysis" — the process used to transform waste plastic into
oil. Pyrolysis heats material in the absence of oxygen so nothing burns. The microwave heat breaks
molecular bonds instead of incinerating the plastic, extracting a simple hydrocarbon liquid.

[PyOil barrel]

PyOil has a 68% lower carbon footprint than virgin crude oil

## Industries we serve

Built for operators with continuous plastic waste streams.

[Manufacturing facility]
[Distribution center]
[Medical facility]
[Waste haulers and MRFs]

Resynergi turns waste to value for:
* Material recovery facilities
* Distribution & fulfillment centers
* Manufacturers
* Medical
* Construction
* Food & beverage processors
* Retail & big-box backrooms
* Agriculture
* Municipal & regional governments
* Event venues
* Automotive
* …And more

## Your plastic waste is costing you money. Resynergi makes it earn money.

Your waste becomes a revenue stream.

More revenue. Less landfill.

Save money. Simplify everything.

[Resynergi AMP Module on truck]

Before

✕Paying tipping fees for landfill
✕Labor tied up with compacting and bailing trash
✕Contributing to ground & water pollution

With Resynergi

✓Waste becomes valuable PyOil — a revenue stream
✓Frees up space and speeds up throughput
✓Reduces carbon in atmosphere & poisons in the landfill

## It's so simple it fits on the back of a truck.

Each **Resynergi AMP Module** is a preassembled 5 ton per day solution that arrives by truck.

Benefits of modularity:

Simplifies logistics
Speeds up deployment and permitting
Easy to scale up by adding modules

## See our process in action

See the process of a 5 ton per day **Resynergi AMP Module** being loaded onto a truck. The second
truck contains the utilities for a standard 20 ton per day site (4 Resynergi AMP Modules).

## The closed loop Resynergi model runs so clean it can be operated **indoors.**

[Resynergi AMP Module facility — clean indoor operation]

The Old Way

Large infrastructure investment. Dirty emissions. Massive feedstock requirements far from the
source.

The Resynergi Way

Small investment. Cleaner emissions. Simpler logistics. Advanced recycling, reimagined.

# Partner in Precision Plastic Injection Moulding and Contract Manufacturing

[Plastic Injection Moulding][74]
[Contract Manufacturing][75]
[Medical Solutions][76]
[YouTube video thumbnail]

## Our Services

Rosti is a global partner in advanced plastic manufacturing and end-to-end production solutions.
With deep expertise, strong engineering capabilities, and a clear focus on quality, we support our
customers from concept to finished product.

### [Plastic Injection Moulding][77]

Our team of expert engineers and technicians have been offering precision plastic injection moulding
for over 80 years.

### [Contract Manufacturing][78]

Contract manufacturing for a complete end-to-end service, with the global resources to handle
large-scale projects, combined with flexibility and attention to detail.

### [Medical Solutions][79]

Providing the highest level of standards to meet your requirements on medical production.

### [Manufacturing Support][80]

From product development and design, to supply chain management and distribution, we have the
knowledge and capabilities to provide innovative solutions to the highest levels of accuracy and
reliability.

## Why Rosti?

### [Over 80 Years Expertise][81]

Founded in 1944

### [13 Manufacturing Sites][82]

A global footprint with strategically placed facilities

### [State of the art Innovations Lab][83]

Taking your products ‘from concept to reality

### [Leading Edge Services][84]

From design to delivery and everything in between

## Sustainability Built Into Every Process

As a plastic moulding company and contract manufacturer, Rosti sits at the center of the supply
chain and has a duty and an opportunity to make a positive environmental impact on the plastics
industry.

### 100% Clean Energy

Always use clean energy at all our sites.

### 100% Green Material Option

Always offer alternatives made from recycled or renewable materials

### 100% Recyclable Design options

Challenge all designs to become more sustainable

### 25% Energy Efficiency Improvement

Do more with less energy, targeting a 50% improvement by 2040

# Restoring the Nile. Protecting our future.

We are a growing youth-led environmental movement in South Sudan that not only restores the Nile but
also empowers communities with sustainable solutions to protect it for future generations.

[Join Us][18]

### Our Projects

###### **Plastic-Free Nile**

Monthly riverbank cleanups and recycling hubs to reduce plastic pollution and protect aquatic life.

###### **Eco-Education**

School and community programs on water safety, environmental awareness, and sustainable practices.

Training for women-led businesses to build green livelihoods and empower communities.

###### **Women's Green Enterpreneurship**

[Volunteer for a cleanup][19]
[Support education][20]
[Partner with us][21]

### Why the Nile matters

[a bridge spanning a river with a wooden bridge]
[a bridge spanning a river with a wooden bridge]

### 50+

Volunteers

[Get Involved][22]
[Join Us][23]

The Nile River is the lifeblood of Northeast Africa, sustaining millions with fresh water in an
otherwise arid landscape. Stretching over 6,650 kilometers and flowing through eleven countries, it
enables agriculture, supports thriving fisheries, and serves as a vital transportation artery for
trade and communication. The Nile’s predictable annual flooding historically enriched the soil,
allowing ancient civilizations like Egypt to flourish and develop advanced irrigation and
agricultural techniques. Beyond its economic backbone, the Nile is deeply woven into the history,
culture, and spirituality of the region. It has inspired art, literature, and religious traditions
for millennia, and remains a symbol of resilience and continuity. Today, the river faces challenges
such as water scarcity, pollution, and climate change, making its protection and sustainable
management more crucial than ever for the prosperity and stability of the entire region.

## We are Select Fuel

Select Fuel has developed patented technologies to help solve the global issue of recyclable
products deposited into landfills. Our company specializes in transforming waste into valuable
biofuel. Additionally, we can produce a wide range of fuels on a large scale, specifically for
internal combustion engine (ICE) power plants. These options include biofuel for motorsports and
luxury sports cars, low-carbon aviation fuel, and biofuels tailored for the transportation industry.
[More About us][5]

#### Partnerships:

[][6]

### The Problem:
### Opportunities Missed in Reusing Valuable Commodities

Over one billion used tires are discarded yearly, leading to a missed opportunity for reusing
valuable commodities. This poses a significant environmental risk globally, as most of these tires
end up in landfills.

Additionally, plastic is a rapidly growing manufactured material that does not decompose. This
creates another major problem, as plastic waste accumulates in landfills, oceans, and waterways,
causing the leaching of harmful chemicals, such as BPA, into our food, water, and ultimately into
our bodies.

[Learn More About Recyclable Waste][7]

### Our Solution:
### Reharnessing Valuable Commodities into Biofuel

Rubber tires and plastic waste should now be considered valuable resources. Our patented technology
allows us to convert these once-discarded materials into various biofuels. These biofuels serve as
valuable petrochemical by-products and are used as a fuel source for all Internal Combustion Engine
(ICE) power plants.

### FUTURE ENERGY NOW

# WELCOME TO SEPCO INDUSTRIES

Sepco Industries Company Limited is the proprietor, sole manufacturer and distributor of the
Polypetron™ Gen. 5 Waste Plastic to Fuel Production System. It is a turnkey solution which can be
conveniently assembled onsite at any location that meets our installation requirements and complies
with local regulations.

[Contact][8]

The Founders of Sepco Industries, working as independent researchers with academic support from the
Center of Energy and Fuels from Biomass, Faculty of Science, Chulalongkorn University, have been
actively involved in research and development of pyrolysis technologies since the 1990’s starting
with tire pyrolysis before moving into plastic pyrolysis. They designed and built the Polypetron™
Gen. 1 Waste Plastic to Fuel in 2003. It still functions today.

 

The current Polypetron™ Gen. 5 model has broken new ground in design and innovation, featuring a
fully enclosed, fully continuous system with the capacity to produce 15,000 liters of crude oil
equivalent per day, per module, while disposing of 20,000 kilograms of waste plastic.


Sepco Industries Company Limited was established in September 2018, to commercialize this innovative
technology which has been in research and development for decades.

About Us

##### THE PLASTIC CRISIS

An estimated 6.3 billion tons of plastic waste had been generated as of 2015, of which only 9% was
recycled. If current plastic production and waste management trends continue, 12 billion tons of
plastic will be in landfills and the natural environment by 2050.


Global plastic production was reported to be around 299 million metric tons in 2013, increasing to
335 million metric tons in 2016.  


It has been calculated that 275 million metric tons of plastic waste was generated in 192 coastal
countries in 2010, with up to 12.7 million tons entering the ocean in a single year. Following this
trend, the total weight of plastic in the oceans will exceed the weight of fish by 2050.


The United Nations reported that the approximate environmental damage caused by plastic to marine
ecosystems comes to 13 billion US Dollars.

Planet Plastic
[Polypetron logo Final silver.png]

The Polypetron™ Gen. 5 applies pyrolysis technology for converting waste plastics into high quality
low-carbon fuel using an innovative continuous process which produces no pollution whatsoever. Our
flagship PPT20 model is able to convert 20 tons of waste plastic into 15,000 liters of pyrolysis
crude oil which is equivalent to sweet or light crude, but of superior quality due to low bitumen
content. Our crude oil equivalent product can be used to power low-speed diesel engines, or be
further refined to produce alternative diesel, gasoline and kerosene.


Viability of our business and production model has been proven with genuine use cases, both through
the sale of pyrolysis fuel oil for industrial machinery and agricultural equipment, and the diesel
produced being provided for testing to the BMTA – one of the largest bus companies in Thailand.
Independent fuel analysis testing has proven our fuel to be of superior quality. Key markets for our
fuel include the shipping industry, and oil traders and refineries due to the high alternative
diesel yield it delivers and its qualification as "advanced biofuel".


[Learn more][9]

The Polypetron

##### THE SEPCO TEAM

Sepco Industries Co., Ltd. is headed up by a veritable who's who in the Petroleum and Energy sector
of Thailand and supported by esteemed and distinguished engineers and academics of the highest
caliber along with leaders in the banking and finance sector and numerous other industries. 


The Founders of Sepco Industries Co., Ltd. have enjoyed academic support from The Center of Fuels
and Energy from Biomass, Faculty of Science, Chulalongkorn University in their pyrolysis research.
At the National Competition of New Business in 2011, our Chief Engineer received a Gold Medal from
the Ministry of Science and Technology for “Car Tires Pyrolysis”.

The Team

# The New Atomic Age

## Valar Atomics is scaling nuclear energy for heavy industrial power and clean hydrocarbon fuel
## production.

[Contact us][7]

# Nuclear needs scale.

Since its invention, nuclear has been a bespoke, project-based industry, constrained by the grid. To
realize the promise of the nuclear age, we need to scale **beyond the grid.**

# A New Model for Nuclear

To unlock economies of scale, we're building hundreds of nuclear reactors on Valar Atomics
gigasites. We focus on grid-independent products: hydrogen, data center power, heavy industrial
power, and clean hydrocarbon fuels.

[Our Technology][8]

# Proven Technology

Our reactor uses high-temperature gas reactor (HTGR) design principles. This architecture has an
unmatched safety profile and proliferation resistance when paired with TRISO fuel.

Fuel

## Triso

Moderator

## Graphite

Coolant

## Helium

# Products

Our high volume, grid-independent products create the cashflow to drive manufacturing excellence and
operational scale. With scale, nuclear will become the cheapest and most reliable source of energy
in the world.

Hydrogen

When paired with our sulfur-iodine cycle process, our reactors produce cheap and abundant hydrogen.

Data Center Power

AI models will require over 200 terawatt hours of additional grid power by 2030. Only nuclear can
meet the demand.

Industrial Power

Gigasites will be home to diverse location-agnostic industrial needs, divorcing green steel and
bauxite electrolysis from the traditional grid model.

Clean Fuel

Combining our cheap hydrogen with captured CO2 from coal/natural gas plants, DAC, and other point
capture sources, we'll create a broad spectrum of hydrocarbons via a modified Fischer-Tropsch
process.

[Ward 250]

## Ward 250

[Partner 1][Partner 2][Partner 3][Partner 4]

Four executive orders gave Valar a mandate to test our reactor. We’re partnering with the Department
of Energy, San Rafael Energy Research Center and the State of Utah to go live before America’s 250th
birthday on July 4th, 2026.

[Learn More][9]

# Unlocking Abundant Energy

Western civilization was built on abundant energy. Coal powered the Industrial Revolution, oil
fueled global commerce, and together, they built the modern world.

Our future—from AI to interplanetary colonization—requires energy at an unprecedented scale and
density. This is the dawn of a new atomic age.

# reimagine-waste

# Working to create a
# world without waste

Only 9% of post-use plastic is recycled. Brightmark’s Plastics Renewal® technology turns the rest
into usable hydrocarbons—creating a new domestic resource from material that would otherwise go to
waste.

## Our solutions

Our process produces two feedstocks: PyBright pyrolysis oil and CarbonBright. These products can be
used as circular petrochemical feedstocks to create new, circular products.

[PyBright][6]
[CarbonBright][7]

## Plastics Brightmark can recycle

[HDPE Circle]

### High-density polyethylene

Opaque, strong, and durable, commonly used for milk jugs, detergent bottles, and shampoo bottles.
[LDPE Circle]

### Low-density polyethylene

Flexible and thin, used for plastic bags, dry cleaning bags, and food wraps.
[PP Circle]

### Polypropylene

Strong, heat-resistant, and rigid. Used for food containers (yogurt, margarine), medicine bottles,
and straws.
[PS Circle]

### Polystyrene

Can be rigid (disposable cutlery) or foam (styrofoam). Known for poor recyclability and low melting
points.
[Misc Circle]

### Other

Other types of plastics.

## Plastics Renewal® Technology

Brightmark’s Plastics Renewal® technology uses a patented-pyrolysis process to convert post-use
plastics into the building blocks needed to create new, circular products—including new plastics.

 

## Plastics recycling programs

Through our strategic partnerships, we’ve developed recycling programs focused on recycling
difficult-to-recycle post-use plastics used in a variety of industries.

bottles, and more.

plastics generated from everyday school activities.

plastic items to flexible films.

We have two circularity centers: A center in Ashley, Indiana, and one in development in Thomaston,
Georgia.

## A responsible end market for post-use plastics

Responsible end markets (REMs)¹ are entities that purchase and use recycled materials to create new
products and are key for responsible recycling².

**Definitions vary by state, but REMs are required to be:**
* Transparent
* Environmentally-sound
* In compliance with laws
* Achieve a minimum yield

 

¹Recycled Materials Association
²PackagingDive: Prioritizing end markets key to taming EPR tension: PPRC speakers

We teamed up with the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary to properly recycle marine
waste—diverting it from landfills and oceans. This first-of-its-kind partnership focuses on keeping
our oceans clean and paving the way for future collaborations focused on circularity.

[Read More][14]

# Powering the

## The proven recycling technology for plastics

Plastic Energy is transforming the global landscape of plastic waste. Our recycling process converts
end-of-life plastic into feedstock used to replace fossil oils in the production of new plastics,
while diverting plastic waste from landfill and incineration.

[Learn more about us][14]

## The plastic problem

1.8B

1.8 billion tonnes of GHG emissions generated by plastics lifecycle.

390M+

Every year more than 390 million tonnes of plastic are produced globally.

22M+

More than 22 million tonnes of plastic waste leak into the environment and oceans yearly.

9%

Globally, only 9% of plastic waste is recycled, 50% is landfilled, 22% is mismanaged and 19%

## The proven recycling technology for plastics

Plastic Energy is transforming the global landscape of plastic waste. Our recycling process converts
end-of-life plastic into feedstock used to replace fossil oils in the production of new plastics,
while diverting plastic waste from landfill and incineration.

## The plastic problem

1.8B

incinerated.

With our patented process, plastics are heated in the absence of oxygen to form hydrocarbon vapours.
These vapours are then condensed into our recycled feedstock – TACOIL™.

[Learn more about us][15]

# Our Story

Eco Fuel Technology, Inc. was founded in 2012 by Swaminathan Ramesh and Himat Taank. The founders
formed the company to focus on manufacturing portable machines that convert waste plastics,
specifically non-reusable, “end-of-life” plastics into reusable diesel fuel.

 

Shortly after formation, Eco Fuel Technology, Inc. worked with James Holm to pilot a portable
machine for installation on a boat. The objective of the pilot project is to install a machine on a
boat that will pick up plastics in the ocean and convert the plastics to diesel fuel while at sea. 

 

Eco Fuel Technology is also partnering with Ocean Guardian (https://www.oceanguardian-og.org/) and
with [Ocean Recovery Systems][16] to recover plastics from the mid depths of the ocean and convert
them to fuel

 

In addition to the pilot project, Eco fuel Technology has launched several collaborative research
studies with universities based in California, Illinois and North Carolina. 

 

Eco Fuel Technology is now working on a number of projects (starting in second and third quarter of
2020):
* a 20 to 60 TPD operation in Memphis, TN
* 60 TPD operation in Alabama
* 60 TPD plant for BC, Canada
* a hugely potential collaboration in Philippines
* set up a manufacturing facility in Thailand to supply the Southeast Asia and Australia
* collaboration with Sunyani Energy, Inc and USABionergy, Inc.

# Our Story

Eco Fuel Technology, Inc. was founded in 2012 by Swaminathan Ramesh and Himat Taank. The founders
formed the company to focus on manufacturing portable machines that convert waste plastics,
specifically non-reusable, “end-of-life” plastics into reusable diesel fuel.

 

Shortly after formation, Eco Fuel Technology, Inc. worked with James Holm to pilot a portable
machine for installation on a boat. The objective of the pilot project is to install a machine on a
boat that will pick up plastics in the ocean and convert the plastics to diesel fuel while at sea. 

 

Eco Fuel Technology is also partnering with Ocean Guardian (https://www.oceanguardian-og.org/) and
with [Ocean Recovery Systems][16] to recover plastics from the mid depths of the ocean

## Solving the problem of plastic waste

## Mission Statement

To solve the global problem of plastic waste which will reduce the environmental impact of plastic
waste and restore ecological balance worldwide.

## Vision Statement

To provide a solution to the global problem of plastic waste by building plastic to fuel conversion
plants worldwide. Establish PlastikGas® USA, PlastikGas® of Latin America and PlastikGas® Europe and
to have 100 or more plants built worldwide by 2030.

# About K-Jet Specialists

[K-Jet Specialists][32] About K-Jet Specialists

**Please email me about anything you need or want to know.** I have lots of parts including exchange
reconditioned Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators available, Auxiliary Air Slides, Auxiliary
Air Valves, D-Jet Manifold Pressure Sensors, Mechanical fuel injection pumps and much more for your
classic European car.

#### Reconditioning Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators since 1993
#### All Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators are sold on an exchange basis. We need your old
#### one back to continue our business and to supply to the next person who needs one**.**

**12 Month Guarantee on parts and workmanship (unless damaged by dirt and/or water in the fuel). We
rebuild our Fuel Distributors and Warm-Up Regulators with many parts, custom made for us, so that
our remanufactured parts meet the highest standards.
**
**We can recondition your own part if you want this to be done.**
**Fuel Distributors can be up-rated for extra power and performance on request.**

**We want your old Fuel Distributors and Warm-up Regulators. Contact us to tell us what you have.**

All Fuel Distributors tested on our Bosch KDJE-P 200 flow benches, our Warm-Up Regulators are set to
Bosch original Specifications on our bespoke test bench.

All our parts are sold on an exchange basis, unless we are reconditioning your own part. We need
your old part back so that we can recondition it for the next person in your situation, needing a
reconditioned part. So please don’t delay in returning your old part.

**All prices are in Australian dollars**

We use the best quality seals which are compatible with all fuels, although we do recommend avoiding
ethanol based fuels where possible. But we also build fuel distributors for racing cars that run e85
and our seals are totally fine with that fuel.

Many of our seals are not ‘off the shelf’ but are made for us to our specification. Our diaphragm
material is also made for us and we have diaphragms for our KE fuel distributors and KE Fuel
distributor kits are pre-shaped for better immediate function.

Colin has been a mechanic since 1973 and has specialised in European cars since 1979 when he moved
to London, England.

In 1990 Colin moved back to Australia and continued servicing European Cars.

In answering the demand for someone with a solid knowledge of the K-Jetronic fuel injection system,
Colin began reconditioning Fuel distributors and Warm-up regulators for other mechanics and offering
them technical help in diagnosing fuel injection problems.

Initially trading under the name ‘Agape Autos’, K-Jet Specialists has been reconditioning K-Jetronic
Fuel Distributors and Warm-up Regulators, and KE-Jetronic Fuel Distributors since 1993.

We also recondition D-Jet MPS, Auxiliary air slides, auxiliary air valves and mechanical petrol
injection systems. We have the experience and ability to recondition almost any part, so if you are
restoring a classic European car and can’t find a part, we may be able to recondition it for you.
Let us know what you need and we will try to help you.

Each part receives a serial number so that we can trace it’s history, when it was reconditioned,
when it was sold and where it went.

Over the years we have sold reconditioned parts to many countries including Australia, Austria,
Bahrain, Belgium, Bolivia, Bratislava, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, China, Columbia, Cyprus, Czech
Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, Egypt, England, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Guatamala,
Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Kazakhstan, Korea, Kuwait,
Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Peru, Philippines,
Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Romania, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Slovakia, , Slovenia, South
Africa, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, UAE, Ukraine, USA. So we are happy to send to you,
wherever you are.

### from waste management to 
### resource management

## harnessing the power of
##  chemical recycling

[][6]

a clean, circular alternative

to landfilling, incineration and mechanical recycling

Misson

Neowaste   converts hard-to-recycle plastic waste (i.e., mixed, contaminated, dirty, co-molded, etc)
and other contaminated waste streams into low sulfur fuel products using a proprietary molecular
reformation process called Polycrack Technology. 

 

We were established to help companies and municipalities meet their sustainability goals when it
became clear that traditional mechanical recycling markets were collapsing and millions of tons of
recyclable materials were being sent to landfills--all as a result of contamination.


Contamination isn't a problem for Neowaste.  We don't recycle mechanically.  We recycle molecularly.
 And while the process description can get a bit technical, the science behind what we do is really
straightforward:


#### Plastic is made from oil. We're simply reversing the process and extracting the oil out of the
#### plastic.

Powered by

[Polycrack Logo.png]
[Learn more ][7]

## Services

[Core Competencies.png]

## The Mission

###### To make recycling more accessible and more sustainable. 

###### Reduce waste disposal costs

Waste disposal costs are on the rise, reaching up to $300 per ton in certain parts of the US. 

 

Neowaste's chemical recycling solution enables us to provide a more sustainable waste management
solution at a significantly lower cost than traditional methods of landfilling, incineration and
mechanical recycling.

 

Environmentally and economically sustainable.

[teal reduce waste costs.png]

###### Divert waste from landfills

Communities and businesses send thousands of tons of recyclable materials to landfills and
incineration facilities each day because of contamination.

 

But contamination is not an issue for Neowaste.  In fact, the technology we use was designed to
manage waste just as it comes--mixed, dirty and full of moisture. 

 

No sorting, cleaning or drying required. 

[teal zero landfill.png]

###### Generate fuel from alternative sources

Most people in the industry like to think of us as a mini-refinery.  Instead of using crude oil as a
feedstock, we use waste.  

 

Neowaste is not only committed to supplying a low sulfur fuel product that exceeds most fuel
acceptance standards, but we are also committed to supplying it at a cost that's competitive with
Platts benchmark pricing.


Fuel specs available upon request.

[teal waste to fuel.png]

## Benefits

[Icon image.png]

## ABOUT

Neowaste is decentralizing waste management through chemical recycling.  

 

By establishing a distributed network of small, modular units, we can manage waste at or near the
source of generation, ultimately reducing the cost of transporting and managing that waste.  


Although we can extract the most fuel from plastic waste, our process is robust enough to process
any material with hydrogen and carbon.  This means we can process almost any type of waste on the
planet and keep those valuable resources out of our oceans and landfills--all while creating
a renewable, low-sulfur fuel product. 

ABOUT

## POLYCRACK TECHNOLOGY

  [Stacked area chart of shares of egg production in the United Kingdom by housing system
  (free-range, cages, barns) from 1996 to 2025 where free-range rises from 10% in 1996 to 75% in
  2025, with cages declining and barns remaining a small share. Source: Defra (2023, 2026). License:
  CC BY.]
  
  Today
  
  ### Three-quarters of eggs produced in the United Kingdom are free-range
  
  Hannah Ritchie and Pablo Rosado
  
  Growing up in the United Kingdom in the 1990s and early 2000s, almost all the eggs in our
  supermarket came from battery hens, those raised in small wire enclosures.
  
  The living conditions in these cages are terrible. Birds get the space equivalent of an A4 sheet
  of paper. They don’t have the room to carry out their natural behaviors, such as nesting,
  perching, or dust bathing.
  
  That has changed in recent decades. You can see this in the chart, which shows the conditions
  under which eggs are produced in the UK. Free-range eggs have increased from just 10% to 75%.
  
  The use of caged hens has fallen, and the types of caged enclosures have also changed. Battery
  cages were banned in 2012, so legally, all cages since then have been “enriched” ones, which
  provide slightly more space. Still, these do not give hens the freedom and room they’d have in
  barns or free-range farms. Studies suggest that moving hens from enriched cages to cage-free
  systems reduces the time they spend in pain by more than half.
  
  And given that most eggs in the UK are now free-range, it’s possible to reduce this pain even
  further.

# Plastics Industry

## A Look at Plastics

The term “plastic” encompasses a broad range of materials. In addition, each has its own special
properties and variations when it comes to properties such as hardness, heat tolerance, and
resiliency. Nonetheless, each of them is made of organic condensation or addition polymers and can
be made into fibers, films, or objects.

There are [7 main types of plastics][5], anything from PET, used in food containers, to PVC, used in
pipes and flooring. Basically, plastics are everywhere in our modern world.

The plastics industry is a [very large industry][6] when many facets and worldwide reach. What is
expected from the plastics industry in [2023 and 2024][7].

* [Plastic Processing Methods][8]
* [Plastics and the Environment][9]
* [The Benefits of Plastic][10]
* [Types of Plastics:][11]
  * [Starting with the letter A][12]
  * [Starting with the letters C, D and E][13]
  * [Starting with the letters F, M and N][14]
  * [Starting with the letter P][15]
  * [Starting with the letters S, T and U][16]

* [Employment and Jobs in the Plastics Industry][19]

* [Synthetic Rubber][21]
* [Recycling Plastics][22]
* [Plastic-eating Bacteria][23]

 


**Classifying Plastics**

There are many methods used to classify plastics. The most common method is to classify them
according to their polymer backbone. Plastics can, however, also be classified according to the
glass transition temperature or thermoplastic versus thermoset.

No matter the classification, [all plastics][24] are polymers, which is a long chain of atoms that
are bonded to one another. These chains are comprised of monomers, which are repeating molecular
units. Most plastics are made of carbon polymers or carbon polymers combined with nitrogen, oxygen,
sulfur, or chlorine in the backbone, which is the main path linking the units together. Plastic is
then customized by “hanging” different molecular groups to the backbone.


**History of Plastic**

Experiments with plastic have been performed for centuries. In fact, even the Old Testament makes
reference to natural materials that were used in the same way as plastic is used today. The exact
year when plastic was first created or discovered, however, is a matter of dispute because the term
“plastic” is so loosely defined.

The discovery of ebonite, or hard [rubber][25], in 1851, however, had a major impact on the plastics
industry. Ebonite was the first thermosetting material to be prepared that also involved its own
unique chemical modification of naturally occurring material. Yet, it took several years for ebonite
to be used to its potential.

As rubber technology was further being developed, collodion was also being manufactured. Collodion
is a cellulose solution that is part of an alcohol-ether mixture. Alexander Parkes, an English
inventor, noticed that a solid residue was left after solvent in the collodion evaporated. In his
word, this residue was a “hard, horny elastic and waterproof substance.” He later patented the
process in 1856 in order to waterproof woven fabrics.

In 1862, a new formulation was unveiled at the Great Exhibition in London. This early plastic was
created by dissolving cellulose nitrate in a solvent. After being placed on a heated rolling
machine, the mixture could be shaped. The first company to dedicated to manufacturing products from
the material, the Parkesine Company, was established in 1866. The company failed, however, in 1868.
A year later, the Xylonite Company was opened by Daniel Spill, who was an associate of Parkes. This
company also went bankrupt in 1874.

In the United States, [plastic compounds][26] were also on the rise. John Wesley Hyatt experimented
with cellulose nitrate in the 1860s. In 1865, he became involved in developing a method for creating
billiard balls with alternative materials. He developed balls made of ivory dust, cloth, and
shellac, which was covered with a collodion coating.

Wyatt and his brother, Isaiah, went on to create a process for producing a material made of camphor
and cellulose nitrate in 1870. By 1872, the term “celluloid” had been coined for the product. The
brothers went on to establish the Celluloid Manufacturing Company, which was later renamed the
American Cellulose Chemical Corporation and was ultimately absorbed by the Celanese Corporation.

By the 1900s, the use of [plastic][27] and all of its variations took off. Today, it is the most
used material in the United States industry, with nearly every product containing plastic in one way
or another.

## Pyrolysis Waste To Energy

Pyrolysis plants can efficiently convert various organic wastes (plastics, tires) into useful
resources – pyrolysis oil, carbon black, synthesis gas. It decomposes organic matter by high
temperature heating in an oxygen-free or low-oxygen environment, reducing the landfill and
incineration of solid waste.

## Biomass Pyrolysis

Biomass pyrolysis plant can convert waste biomass into high-value biochar. It provides sustainable
solutions for agriculture, energy and environmental protection. Biomass carbonization plants are
widely used in wood charcoal making, straw charcoal making, rice husk charcoal making, coconut shell
charcoal making, sawdust charcoal making and bamboo charcoal making.

### Ensure Safe Disposal of Any Waste Stream

#### No Solid Waste

#### No Waste Water

#### No Waste Gas

Solid waste will come from the particulars in the in dust collector, which can be made into pellet
for furthe carbonization and dust in the dedusting scrubber, non-pollution, can be burried directly.

No waste water produced. Water will be recycled to be used for cooling the condensers, biochar water
cooling discharging screw and flue condensers.

Gas will go through the cleaning system, including dust collectors, extra syngas burning system,
dedusting scrubber and activated carbon and UV light unit to be released.

# We recycle
# "unrecyclable"
# plastic

Resynergi converts waste plastic that has traditionally been landfilled or incinerated into valuable
PyOil, a feedstock for new, high quality plastic products.

## Plastic waste Resynergi will take:

[HDPE plastic products] [HDPE recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #2

High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE)

Common Products

Milk jugs, shampoo bottles, patio chairs

[LDPE plastic products] [LDPE recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #4

Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE)

Common Products

Grocery bags, shrink film, flexible packaging

[PP plastic products] [PP recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #5

Polypropylene (PP)

Common Products

Yogurt cups, bottle caps, straws, medicine bottles

[PS plastic products] [PS recycling symbol]

Plastic Code #6

Polystyrene (PS)

Common Products

Styrofoam cups, egg cartons, disposable cutlery

The Problem

The above categories represent the **majority** of post-consumer plastic waste.

## Only 9% of plastic waste gets recycled today.

We're here to change that.

0%

Predicted increase
in global plastic waste by 2060

OECD, 2022 Report

The Solution

What is PyOil?

PyOil is a liquid hydrocarbon that can be used as a drop-in replacement for crude oil, to make new
plastic. The name comes from the word "pyrolysis" — the process used to transform waste plastic into
oil. Pyrolysis heats material in the absence of oxygen so nothing burns. The microwave heat breaks
molecular bonds instead of incinerating the plastic, extracting a simple hydrocarbon liquid.

[PyOil barrel]

PyOil has a 68% lower carbon footprint than virgin crude oil

## Industries we serve

Built for operators with continuous plastic waste streams.

[Manufacturing facility]
[Distribution center]
[Medical facility]
[Waste haulers and MRFs]

Resynergi turns waste to value for:
* Material recovery facilities
* Distribution & fulfillment centers
* Manufacturers
* Medical
* Construction
* Food & beverage processors
* Retail & big-box backrooms
* Agriculture
* Municipal & regional governments
* Event venues
* Automotive
* …And more

## Your plastic waste is costing you money. Resynergi makes it earn money.

Your waste becomes a revenue stream.

More revenue. Less landfill.

Save money. Simplify everything.

[Resynergi AMP Module on truck]

Before

✕Paying tipping fees for landfill
✕Labor tied up with compacting and bailing trash
✕Contributing to ground & water pollution

With Resynergi

✓Waste becomes valuable PyOil — a revenue stream
✓Frees up space and speeds up throughput
✓Reduces carbon in atmosphere & poisons in the landfill

## It's so simple it fits on the back of a truck.

Each **Resynergi AMP Module** is a preassembled 5 ton per day solution that arrives by truck.

Benefits of modularity:

Simplifies logistics
Speeds up deployment and permitting
Easy to scale up by adding modules

## See our process in action

See the process of a 5 ton per day **Resynergi AMP Module** being loaded onto a truck. The second
truck contains the utilities for a standard 20 ton per day site (4 Resynergi AMP Modules).

Video

## The closed loop Resynergi model runs so clean it can be operated **indoors.**

[Resynergi AMP Module facility — clean indoor operation]

The Old Way

Large infrastructure investment. Dirty emissions. Massive feedstock requirements far from the
source.

The Resynergi Way

Small investment. Cleaner emissions. Simpler logistics. Advanced recycling, reimagined.
